chief_complaint: Uncontrolled stage 2 hypertension with associated cardiovascular risk factors
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 57-year-old woman with a long-standing history of obesity, essential hypertension diagnosed in 2018, and prediabetes. Blood pressure remains elevated (143/105 mmHg) despite low‑dose lisinopril. She reports chronic low‑back pain and knee osteoarthritis, for which she uses naproxen sodium, contributing to ongoing NSAID exposure. Anemia has been present since 2008 without recent laboratory follow‑up. Since August 2020 she transitioned to full‑time employment, reporting increased stress. Persistent transportation barriers and limited recent outpatient visits (last visit May 2021) have likely impeded optimal disease monitoring and management.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include prior unemployment, part‑time employment, dental disease (gingivitis, caries, gingival disease) resolved between 2018‑2019, a streptococcal sore throat treated in 2018, and limited social contact resolved in 2017. A past miscarriage (1985) is noted. Medication review entries were completed in 2019 and 2020.

active_medications.name: naproxen sodium 220 MG Oral Tablet
active_medications.purpose: Pain control for osteoarthritis of the knee and chronic musculoskeletal pain

social_determinants: Long‑standing lack of reliable transportation and documented transport problems limit access to care. The patient has full‑time employment since August 2020, reports occupational stress, and has a higher education background. No smoking or alcohol data are available.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure: stage 2 hypertension (143/105 mmHg). BMI data missing but obesity is documented. Prediabetes (A1c 5.9%). No lipid panel available; ASCVD risk likely elevated. Chronic anemia present. Comorbidity flags confirm hypertension, anemia, and osteoarthritis. Charlson index 1, clinical complexity moderate.

clinical_impression: The patient presents with uncontrolled hypertension in the context of obesity, prediabetes, chronic musculoskeletal pain, and anemia, compounded by social barriers to care. Current therapy is insufficient for blood pressure control and may increase renal and gastrointestinal risk due to NSAID use. Comprehensive risk factor mitigation, medication optimization, and addressing social determinants are needed.
